top_items.summary: A merged fix stops eight writer code paths in gateway platform plugins from recreating a deleted or renamed profile home via raw mkdir(parents=True) calls. All affected writers now go through mkdir_under_hermes_home, with per-adapter handling retained: Google Chat in-memory counts are skipped, Feishu comment pairing raises rather than falsely reporting a save, and Matrix crypto/recovery-key writes are refused through existing warning and abort paths. top_items.content_html:
fix(profiles): platform adapters never recreate a deleted profile home

Eight writers in gateway platform plugins still created their directory with a

raw mkdir(parents=True) under the active profile home. An adapter bound to a

named profile that was deleted or renamed meanwhile brought profiles/<name>/

back on its next write (tracker #155595 U3, part 2 of #9).

They now go through mkdir_under_hermes_home; each keeps its existing handling:

  • Google Chat thread-count store: skipped, counts stay in memory;
  • Feishu comment pairing: raises, so an approval is never reported saved;
  • Matrix crypto store (connect and E2EE setup) and recovery-key target and

write: refused through the existing reason / warning / abort paths;

line-neutral (the adapter is over the 2000-line cap);

  • the auth.json lock helper (_file_lock): raises before a lock file is created;

Photon's stores take it before writing, so the lock recreated a renamed home

first. Line-neutral (auth.py is over the cap);

  • Photon auth.json: raises to the auth caller;
  • Photon sidecar mirror: falls back to the source dir like a read-only one;
  • WhatsApp secondary bridge-port record: raises into connect's existing

OSError handling;

  • WhatsApp Cloud inbound media cache: the media is dropped like a failed

write.

Each gets a delete+rename regression that fails on main and on a raw-mkdir

mutant.

top_items.content:
3-day kernel grinding retrospective with 3x RTX 6000 Pro and Oh-My-Hermes

- Fixed SGLang ignoring the DSA dense prefill config on SM120
- Fixed Qwen3.6 AWQ crashing on load when modules_to_not_convert was specified
- Fixed engine crashes when swapping AWQ/GPTQ model weights by writing a custom Marlin inverse transform — bit-exact across 44 test cases (#52330)
- Fixed Qwen3-Coder tool-call constraints breaking over a single whitespace mismatch (violations dropped from 10/10 to 0/15)
- Fixed memory release right after pause getting rejected 29 out of 40 times
- Blocked path traversal on /start_profile (#52351)
- Fixed Triton main failing to even compile on glibc 2.35
- Cleaned up Triton tests failing to meet the 99KB SM120 smem limit
- Fixed FlashInfer SM120 FMHAv2 concurrent JIT build race condition (crashes dropped from 19/40 to 0)
- Verified someone else's PR on our cards for vLLM allocating 2x KV cache (25.6GB to 12.3GB) and left a confirmation comment
- Tried switching GDN decode to FlashInfer, but it's already memory-bandwidth bound (0.96–0.99x) — left the benchmarks and dropped it

Thought 3 GPUs meant I could run TP3, but modern models all have power-of-2 head counts so it doesn't divide evenly. Ended up using the 3 cards strictly for PP/DP.

From issue hunting and repros to fixes and PRs, OMH assigned one GPU per task and ran everything in parallel yielding an output I never could have pulled off solo.

top_items.content:
OpenAI published its internal pretraining loss numbers, the kind of thing labs usually keep to themselves.

In a post by chief scientist Jakub Pachocki, log-perplexity on OpenAI's held-out code set goes from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to 0.91 for GPT-4. A model at around 0.76 is the one that started producing what he calls groundbreaking results on open math problems. He expects the next jump somewhere in the 0.68 to 0.7 window and says he doesn't know what those capabilities will be.

What he's asking for is common limits across labs, measured this way, that nobody crosses until we can actually understand and monitor what these models are doing.

Kind of wild that the number everyone was guessing about fits in two decimal places.
